exercise.name: Cable Neutral Grip Wide Pulldown

reference.title: Cable Neutral Grip Wide Pulldown (version 2)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

equipment: Wide neutral-grip (parallel-handle) lat bar, modelled as two D-handles on one cable
exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder adduction and extension, scapular depression, elbow flexion)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull the bar down to the upper chest, breathe in as it rises.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, short pause, about 2 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can pull to the upper chest without swinging back.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; 1 s pause at the chest

cues.text: Sit under the high pulley, feet flat, and take the wide parallel handles with the palms facing each other, hands a little wider than the shoulders; arms long overhead, chest up.
Breathe out; draw the shoulders down and pull the handles to the top of the chest, elbows driving down and slightly forward of the trunk, leaning back only a little.
Handles beside the upper chest, elbows under the hands and close to the ribs, chest up to meet them.
Breathe in and let the handles rise under control until the arms are long and the shoulders lift slightly.
Brief stretch at the top, then pull again.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning far back and rowing the bar
mistakes.fix: Keep the lean small (about 10-15 degrees back) and pull down, not back.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the elbows flare straight out to the sides
mistakes.fix: With the palms facing, let the elbows come down slightly in front of the body, close to the ribs.

mistakes.mistake: Using momentum to swing the weight down
mistakes.fix: Control the whole rep; lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the bar fly up and the shoulders shrug at the top
mistakes.fix: Let the bar rise slowly with the arms long but the shoulders controlled.

kinematics.setup: Neutral (palms facing), 60 cm between the hands (shoulders 40 cm apart)
kinematics.norm: Neutral (palms facing) about 1.3-1.5 times shoulder width (clinical opinion); in EMG studies grip width and hand orientation changed lat activity only modestly (Signorile 2002; Lehman 2004)
From nearly straight to about 90-120 degrees (clinical opinion)
From arms overhead to the elbows by the sides (clinical opinion)
Small backward lean, about 10-15 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 1.2 s down, 0.4 s at the chest, 2 s up
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Neutral Grip Wide Pulldown (version 2), video (movement reference)
Signorile, Zink & Szwed 2002, a comparative electromyographical investigation of muscle utilization patterns using various hand positions during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 16(4):539-546)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the shoulder or elbow, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control up and down without swinging.
Pull to the front of the chest and keep the head out of the handles' path.
This model sits on a plain box without the machine's thigh pads; with heavy loads use a machine with thigh pads so the body stays down.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort overhead: shorten the top range and keep the elbows a little in front of the body (clinical opinion).
Elbow discomfort: lighten the load and loosen the grip slightly.

muscleNotes.lats_l: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm down and in to the side.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Draw the shoulder blade down and back at the bottom.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Draw the shoulder blade down and back at the bottom.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bends the elbow as the handles come down; the neutral grip shares the work with the brachialis and brachioradialis.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Bends the elbow as the handles come down; the neutral grip shares the work with the brachialis and brachioradialis.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps draw the elbow down and back.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps draw the elbow down and back.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk steady on the seat.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the chest up and the small lean back.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the chest up and the small lean back.

guides.label: Handles down to the upper chest
Elbows well bent at the chest
